headline: 1,484 hospitalised as 5 more die from dengue in 24 hours
summary: The total death toll for the year has reached 176, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
details: Five people died from dengue fever in the last 24 hours, while 1,484 others were admitted to hospitals across the country.
According to a regular notice from the Health Emergency Operation Center and Control Room of the DGHS, the admissions were reported on Thursday (September 17).
The breakdown of hospitalisations includes 227 in Dhaka South City Corporation and 207 in Dhaka North City Corporation, with 190 others in the Dhaka division outside the city corporations.
Other affected regions include Khulna (252), Barishal (211), Chattogram (232), Rajshahi (102), Mymensingh (64), Rangpur (35), and Sylhet (4).
The DGHS reports that the total number of dengue-related deaths in Bangladesh this year has now reached 176.

headline: EC aims to complete Union Parishad polls before June 6 next year
summary: The Election Commission is coordinating with ministries to ensure local government elections do not clash with HSC exams or academic schedules.
details: The Election Commission (EC) aims to complete the Union Parishad elections before June 6, 2025, to avoid clashing with the Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) examination schedule.
Election Commissioner Abul Fazal Md Sanaullah stated that the timeline was discussed during an interdepartmental meeting with heads of 27 ministries and divisions at the EC headquarters in Dhaka.
The commission is considering the impact of recent floods on primary and secondary education, as well as the need for teachers to manage training and duties without disrupting evaluations.
While November and December are packed with annual exams, the EC noted that January may offer some scope for holding the polls.
Sanaullah explained that the schedule is tight because Ramadan begins around February 7 or 8, followed immediately by SSC exams, leaving a narrow window before the HSC exams in June.
The EC will further deliberate on budget planning and staff coordination before announcing the specific dates for the elections.
Separately, the EC announced that the Thakurgaon-1 by-election will be held on October 29, with troop deployment and technology similar to the parliamentary polls.
caption:
Union Parishad elections must be finished by June 6 to avoid clashing with HSC exams.

The Election Commission (EC) aims to complete the Union Parishad elections before June 6, 2025, to avoid clashing with the Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) examination schedule.

Election Commissioner Abul Fazal Md Sanaullah stated that the timeline was discussed during an interdepartmental meeting with heads of 27 ministries and divisions at the EC headquarters in Dhaka.

The commission is considering the impact of recent floods on primary and secondary education, as well as the need for teachers to manage training and duties without disrupting evaluations.

While November and December are packed with annual exams, the EC noted that January may offer some scope for holding the polls.

Sanaullah explained that the schedule is tight because Ramadan begins around February 7 or 8, followed immediately by SSC exams, leaving a narrow window before the HSC exams in June.

The EC will further deliberate on budget planning and staff coordination before announcing the specific dates for the elections.

Separately, the EC announced that the Thakurgaon-1 by-election will be held on October 29, with troop deployment and technology similar to the parliamentary polls.
